title: Semantic HTML vs ARIA: Accessibility First

scenes.say: When building accessible sites, should you use semantic HTML or ARIA roles first?

scenes.label: Native
scenes.sub: Elements like nav, main, and button have built-in meaning.
scenes.say: Semantic elements like nav, main, and button already tell browsers and assistive tech what they are.
Semantic HTML is accessible by default. ARIA adds roles or properties, but needs extra work and should only fill gaps.
A real button is accessible out of the box. A div pretending to be a button needs ARIA and keyboard handling.

scenes.question: Should you use ARIA instead of semantic HTML?
scenes.right: No, always use semantic HTML first. ARIA is for cases where HTML alone can't provide needed accessibility.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Should you use ARIA instead of semantic HTML? The answer is no—always start with semantic elements, and only use ARIA when you can't get there with HTML alone.
